turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. Other people tell me it looks normal, but I feel like it’s the first thing people notice—families, nurses, people at church.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports being unable to stop noticing a perceived sagging, uneven area around the jaw and neck despite reassurance from others that it appears normal.

turns.doctor_question: When others tell you it looks normal, can you consider that they might be right, or are you completely certain the flaw is there?
turns.patient_response: I mean, I hear them, but I don’t really believe it. When I look at my jaw and neck, I see the sagging and unevenness right away. It feels like that’s what people notice first when they look at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient continues to perceive sagging and unevenness of the jaw and neck despite reassurance from others and believes it is highly noticeable to people.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself spending a lot of time doing things like checking mirrors, adjusting your clothes to hide your neck, or touching the area repeatedly?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Before work or a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror to fix my collar and hair around my neck. Then I’ll check my phone camera again. Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s made me late more than once.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeated mirror and phone-camera checking, adjusting collar and hair to conceal the neck, and seeking reassurance from her daughter, causing lateness.

turns.doctor_question: Do you view this sagging as purely a cosmetic flaw, or are you worried it might be a sign of an underlying medical illness?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really thinking it’s an illness. It just looks wrong to me—like it’s sagging more than it should—and I want to hide it.
